decisive_items: His mother had systemic lupus erythematosus treated with hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisolone and was positive for anti-SSa/Ro and anti-SSb/La antibodies
antibody testing confirmed high-titer antinuclear antibodies (>1:1000) and 52-kD anti-SSa/Ro and anti-SSb/La positivity
His heart rate remained between 60 and 100 bpm
response.rationale: Maternal anti-Ro/La antibodies and confirmed neonatal antibodies strongly indicate neonatal lupus, which explains the bradycardia (heart block) and progressive pulmonary disease. Congenital heart block is a component of neonatal lupus, but the broader syndrome fits better. Bronchopulmonary dysplasia is less specific given the antibody evidence.

rejected.why: Ground-glass opacities are nonspecific and occur in neonatal lupus pneumonitis; the antibody profile and cardiac involvement point away from BPD as the primary diagnosis.

Bradycardia is a feature of congenital heart block, but it is a manifestation of neonatal lupus rather than a separate diagnosis; the antibody evidence and pulmonary findings support the broader syndrome.
